Stable paid-tier coding model, generally available on 2026-10-13. Input, thinking and output share 1,048,576 tokens; model output records long-decode capacity up to the remaining window, while the Gemini binding caps current streaming requests at 65,536 tokens. Long decode requires continuation handling, which current Chord does not implement; direct non-streaming REST requests stop at 32,768. Thinking levels are low, medium (default) and high. On the configured Gemini API route, legacy thinking_budget maps to a level with a warning; minimal is unsupported. Explicit caching is unsupported and sampling parameters are ignored. Standard pricing is $4/$20 per million input/output tokens from 2026-12-01, with $2/$10 introductory rates through 2026-11-30. Live smoke checks on 2026-10-14: chord doctor models, gemini preset, wire ID gemini-4-argon, medium level, streaming GenerateContent at https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/. The direct attempt timed out; a subsequent attempt through the existing local SOCKS proxy reached the API but returned HTTP 429 with free-tier quota limit 0 for this model. No completion, low/high variants or long decode were verified. The binding's streaming cap is documentation-backed; the live check is quota-blocked. The 2026-11-13 pricing recheck replaces the percentage-only cache wording with exact implicit cache rates ($0.10/MTok through 2026-11-30 and $0.20/MTok from 2026-12-01) and records that the pricing page lists no separate cache-write or storage fee.

Stable paid-tier coding model, announced 2026-10-28 and generally available to paying API developers on 2026-11-10. Official coding evidence: first on CursorBench 4.0, WANDR and AutomationBench, plus SEC-bench Pro 88.2%, CWE-bench 71.0% and ExploitGym 54.8% from the announcement. Input, thinking and output share 1,048,576 tokens; model output records long-decode capacity up to the remaining window, while the Gemini binding caps current streaming requests at 65,536 tokens as documented on the model page. Thinking levels are low, medium (default) and high. No compaction profile is recorded: neither a long-context reliability window nor a pricing-tier boundary is documented for Carbon, so the entry inherits the global default like Argon. Standard pricing is $4/$20 per million input/output tokens from 2026-12-01, with $2/$10 introductory rates through 2026-11-30 and implicit cache hits at $0.10/$0.20 across the same boundary; explicit caching and the Free tier are unsupported, and Batch, Flex and Priority rates differ. Live smoke check on 2026-11-11: chord doctor models, gemini preset, wire ID gemini-4-carbon, medium level, streaming GenerateContent at https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/, with model settings borrowed from gemini-4-argon because the embedded catalog snapshot does not contain Carbon yet. The request reached the API with the credential attached and returned HTTP 429 with free-tier quota limit 0 for this model; no completion, low/high variants or long decode were verified. A direct GenerateContent call confirmed the same quota-blocked result.

Stable generally available coding model, released 2026-11-12 and rolled out globally on the Gemini API and Google AI Studio (free and paid tiers; the free tier is rate-limited). Official coding evidence: the launch post reports Terminal-Bench 4.1 57% (cheating-adjusted) versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash, the DeepMind Gemini benchmark table records SWE-sweep 13.5% versus Claude Sonnet 5.5 3.1% and GPT-6.1 Terra 5.8%, and the model card lists iterative repository coding and debugging. The API model page records the stable wire ID gemini-4-hydrogen, text/image/video/audio/PDF input, a unified 1,048,576-token window shared by input, thinking and output, and a 65,536-token default synchronous output cap with long decode up to the remaining window. The model fact records long-decode capacity; the Gemini binding caps single requests at 65,536 tokens. Long decode requires background execution or client-side continuation, neither of which current Chord implements; unlike Carbon/Argon, Hydrogen's direct non-streaming REST cap is also 65,536. Thinking is always on at low/medium/high(default)/xhigh; minimal is rejected, thinking_budget is deprecated, sampling parameters are ignored, thought signatures must be passed back, and only implicit caching applies (minimum 4,096 input tokens; explicit caching unsupported). The compaction profile is deliberately omitted: no Hydrogen-specific long-context reliability window or pricing-tier boundary is documented and pricing is flat across the full 1M window, so the entry inherits the global default like Argon and Carbon. The config profile records the documented default thinking level high; documented route behaviors stay in this inventory reason rather than config_profile.compat, consistent with the sibling Gemini 4 entries. Standard pricing is $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens with implicit cache hits at $0.075/MTok; the official pricing page lists no separate cache-write or storage fee, no long-context surcharge and no promotional tier, while Batch, Flex and Priority rates differ. No live endpoint check was run in this session: no Gemini API credential was available to the tooling and the embedded Chord catalog does not contain Hydrogen yet; the binding cap is documentation-backed. Prior gemini smoke checks (2026-10-14 Argon, 2026-11-11 Carbon) reached the API but returned HTTP 429 with free-tier quota limit 0, so no completion, thinking variants or long decode were verified.

The compaction profile mirrors gpt-6.1-sol: 0.25/0.20 triggers at 0.25 x 922,000 = 230,500 tokens, below the 272K tier; no separate long-context quality limit is documented, and the reasoning-summary profile follows the family-level reasoning-guide evidence also cited for gpt-6.1-sol. The codex binding follows the official Codex model documentation (gpt-6.1-terra listed as a recommended model, Codex CLI 0.159.0 or later); the required live smoke check was attempted on 2026-10-27 but returned HTTP 401 on rejected OAuth credentials, with the existing gpt-6.1-sol failing identically, so no completion was verified. The openai binding follows the model documentation; no live check was run because no API credential is available.

Official Tencent Hy4 release of 2026-11-04 with documented software-engineering capability: the launch post names long-horizon software engineering, and the Hy research page records frontend and game-development gains over Hy4 preview (GameDev +19.1%, GameLogic +9.8%) plus first-time computer-use (CLI/GUI). The Hy API guide documents the hy4 wire ID on OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages protocols with 1M context, 960k max input and 64k max output, recorded as the binary reading 1048576/983040/65536 because it is the only one where input and output sum to the context window; the guide's capability description and the TokenHub listing confirm text and image input, with video not listed for hy4. The deep-thinking doc documents thinking enabled by default, toggleable through the native thinking:{type} object, with reasoning_effort default high and no_think to disable. Pricing is the standard Singapore TokenHub USD rate $0.834/$2.501 per million input/output tokens with $0.042 cache hits and no documented cache-write fee (Guangzhou lists the same prices as ¥6/¥18/¥0.3; a 50% TokenHub promotion runs through 2026-12-31 Beijing time and is not the recorded price). No compaction profile is recorded because no long-context reliability window or pricing-tier boundary is documented. No managed binding was added: the TokenHub route has no route-specific variant evidence and no live check was run (no credential).

It stays a candidate and will not be promoted: Tencent Cloud announcement 2559 takes hy4-preview offline on TokenHub, ADP and CloudBase from Beijing time 2026-12-07 00:00:00 and migrates qualifying traffic to hy4, so the official release tencent/hy4 is the runtime-relevant entry.
